analysis:
Reviewed all 13 batch analyses and the supplied source replay. The replay is incomplete (76 of 84 source units omitted), so implementation conclusions in prior analyses cannot be independently validated here. No concrete regression is supported by the replayed changes.

The PR introduces default-on coordinated pair updates: verified staging, bounded admission drains, installation/restart, matching-build replanning and candidate recovery (changelog.d/cluster-auto-update.md:3-10; docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md:536-583). Manual updates install before requesting coordinated restart (docs/provider/cli-reference.md:1804-1809); that ordering already existed for installation and is not independently a new unsafe-write finding. ProviderLoop.swift:566-569 adds drain ownership/task state but does not show its enforcement. Configuration documentation at docs/reference/configuration.md:410 adds the cluster update opt-out.

Cross-batch reports identify mailbox validation, process-bound drain requests, release/phase freshness, verified staging, child-bound restart callbacks and bounded candidate probes. These address earlier local questions, but their source is absent from this replay. Remaining material review should verify ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain admission reopening and native retirement; ClusterPairUpdateCycle peer authentication, exact-release agreement, worker-free fallback and cancellation; and ClusterCandidateRecovery/ClusterMemberSupervisor predecessor integrity, quarantine and heartbeat promotion. Relevant contracts are A-018, T-010, T-043, TB-003 and TB-012/T-060. The same-binary recovery limitation remains documented, not established as newly exploitable.

Restart/replanning must retain current build qualification and fresh connection authorization (A-017, TB-002, TB-011, T-053/T-054); matching versions and --version probes do not establish either. No replayed change alters prompt encryption, key custody, tenant cache scoping (T-041), or billing. Human/source review remains necessary for the omitted update/drain implementations and the threat model's coverage of peer-controlled update coordination; documentation and synthetic-test summaries do not prove those controls.
